source_meta._title: Pointed dripstone can be destroyed by tridents in adventure mode

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition 21w19a in a fresh single-player world running on the integrated server. Use Creative mode with cheats enabled for deterministic item acquisition and target placement, then switch the player to Adventure mode before throwing the trident. Default mouse and keyboard controls are assumed; use the equivalent bound controls if they have been changed.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact affected version 21w19a rather than the fixed version 23w42a or a newer version.
The player must have permission to execute the /gamemode command; in a single-player test world, enable cheats during world creation.
Use an open, level area with enough space to stand several blocks from the target and maintain an unobstructed line of sight.
The player must be standing on the ground rather than flying before switching from Creative mode to Adventure mode.
Have one Pointed Dripstone item and one unenchanted Trident available in separate hotbar slots before entering Adventure mode.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation that uses Java Edition snapshot 21w19a, launch it, and wait for the main menu to finish loading.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is visible and identifies the running version as 21w19a.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, create a new test world, set Game Mode to Creative, ensure cheats are enabled, and create the world. Wait until surrounding terrain has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Allow Cheats: ON -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in a loaded world in Creative mode and can use commands.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Open the Search Items tab, select the search field, enter "pointed dripstone", and move the Pointed Dripstone item from the search results into an empty hotbar slot. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots at the bottom of the inventory.
steps.success_cue: A Pointed Dripstone item is present in one of the nine hotbar slots.

steps.action: While the Creative inventory is open, clear the search field, enter "trident", and move a normal unenchanted Trident into a different empty hotbar slot. Press E again to close the inventory.
steps.success_cue: The inventory is closed, and both Pointed Dripstone and Trident are visible in separate hotbar slots.

steps.action: Stand in an open area and select the Pointed Dripstone hotbar slot by pressing its corresponding number key or scrolling to it. Aim at the top face of a full ground block and press the Use Item/Place Block control, which is right-click by default, once to place the pointed dripstone upright.
steps.exact_input: Pointed Dripstone hotbar slot; right-click the top face of a ground block
steps.success_cue: One upright pointed dripstone spike is visibly attached to the top of the ground block.

steps.action: Move approximately 5 to 8 horizontal blocks away from the placed pointed dripstone. Face the spike and ensure there are no blocks or entities between the player and the target. Remain standing on the ground.
steps.exact_input: W/A/S/D as needed; stop 5-8 blocks from the target
steps.success_cue: The complete pointed dripstone target is visible with a clear, unobstructed throwing path from the player.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat, type the command exactly as shown including the leading slash, and press Enter to switch the player to Adventure mode.
steps.success_cue: The command succeeds and the game displays confirmation that the player's game mode was set to Adventure Mode.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the Trident by pressing the corresponding number key or scrolling until the trident is the active item. Do not use or drop it yet.
steps.exact_input: Number key for the Trident hotbar slot
steps.success_cue: The Trident is highlighted in the hotbar and is visible in the player's hand while the player remains in Adventure mode.

steps.action: Place the crosshair over the thicker body or base section of the pointed dripstone rather than merely beside its narrow tip. Keep the throwing path clear and do not move closer than the prepared throwing position.
steps.exact_input: Mouse movement to aim at the pointed dripstone
steps.success_cue: The center crosshair is directly over the visible pointed dripstone target.

steps.action: Press and hold the Use Item control, which is right-click by default, while keeping the crosshair on the pointed dripstone. Hold it for about one second so the trident reaches a fully charged throwing state.
steps.success_cue: The trident is visibly drawn back and ready to be thrown, with the crosshair still aimed at the pointed dripstone.

steps.action: Release the Use Item control to throw the fully charged trident directly at the pointed dripstone. Make no additional attacks or interactions; wait only until the projectile reaches and impacts the target position.
steps.success_cue: The thrown trident has just contacted the pointed-dripstone target position.

stor.handoff_condition: The Adventure-mode player has just thrown a fully charged trident and the projectile has contacted the position occupied by the placed pointed dripstone. Begin observation immediately, before making another attack or interacting with the target area.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a world seed, coordinates, world type, or a dedicated-server requirement. A fresh single-player world and an open target area are therefore used as practical execution choices.

The report does not state how the items should be obtained. Creative inventory acquisition is used to avoid unrelated crafting, exploration, and combat while preserving the required Adventure-mode state at the time of the throw.

The report says to place "some pointed dripstone" but does not specify a count or arrangement. This plan uses one upright pointed dripstone block because it provides the singular target required by the reported interaction.

The report does not specify a throwing distance or charge duration. A distance of approximately 5 to 8 blocks and a fully charged throw are chosen to provide an unobstructed, moving trident projectile and avoid an undercharged attempt.
The report does not specify custom controls. The plan uses the default Java Edition controls and requires equivalent bound actions if controls have been changed.
